concepts.question: How many small, sharply outlined round red dots, each far smaller than the width of a main retinal vessel, are scattered over the orange retinal background?

none.text: no red dots anywhere on the orange background; the only red structures are the branching vessels themselves

few.text: a handful of red dots, roughly one to five, all lying within one part of the visible retina

moderate.text: red dots easily found in more than one quarter of the retina but still countable, roughly six to twenty in all

many.text: red dots in every quarter of the retina and too many to count singly, more than about twenty per quarter

concepts.question: How many larger red patches with blurred or irregular outlines, clearly bigger than the small round dots, are visible in the retina?

none.text: no red patch is larger or blurrier than the fine round dots; the retina shows dots or nothing at all

few.text: one to about five blurred red patches, confined to one quarter of the visible retina

moderate.text: blurred red patches in two or three quarters of the retina, fewer than about twenty in any one of them

many.text: more than about twenty blurred red patches in each of the four quarters of the retina

concepts.question: How much sharply outlined bright yellow-white deposit, sometimes in clusters, lines or rings, is visible in the retina?

none.text: no yellow-white deposit on the retina; the brightest structure in the frame is the pale optic disc itself

few.text: one or two small yellow-white specks or a single short line, together well under one optic-disc area

moderate.text: several sharp-edged yellow-white clusters or a partial ring, together about one optic-disc area

many.text: yellow-white deposit in rings or confluent sheets covering more than about two optic-disc areas

concepts.question: How many pale greyish-white patches with soft, feathery, ill-defined edges are visible, distinct from the sharply outlined yellow deposits?

none.text: no soft-edged pale patch; any bright lesion present has a crisp yellow border rather than a fuzzy white one

few.text: anything from one up to about five fluffy white patches with feathery margins, however widely they are scattered

many.text: more than about five fluffy white patches with feathery margins, too many to count on one hand

concepts.question: Do the larger dark retinal veins vary in calibre along their course, looking like a string of sausages rather than a smoothly tapering tube?

absent.text: every large vein tapers smoothly from the disc outwards with no local widening or pinching

mild.text: one vein shows a short stretch of alternating widening and narrowing, in one quarter of the retina only

marked.text: definite sausage-string calibre change in veins in two or more of the four quarters of the retina

concepts.question: Are there fine, irregular, tortuous vessel segments lying within the retina, often near red lesions, that do not follow the orderly branching of the main vessels?

absent.text: all visible vessels branch and taper in orderly fashion; no tangled segment sits between them

mild.text: a faint or doubtful tangle of fine intraretinal vessels, hard to tell from a normal small branch

marked.text: prominent tangles of fine irregular intraretinal vessels in one or more of the four quarters of the retina

concepts.question: Taking the optic disc as the centre, in how many quadrants of the visible retina are red lesions present?

none.text: no red dot or patch in any quarter of the retina that the frame actually shows

one_quadrant.text: red lesions in one quarter only, quartering about the disc or, if it is off-frame, the image centre

two_or_three_quadrants.text: red lesions in two or three of the four quarters, with at least one quarter free of them

four_quadrants.text: red lesions in every one of the four quarters of the visible retina, none spared

concepts.question: Is there a fine net, tuft or frond of thin new vessels on or beside the optic disc, or elsewhere along the vascular arcades, distinct from the normal branching vessels?

absent.text: every vessel runs out from the disc along the arcades and tapers; no extra net lies on the disc or retinal surface

present.text: a fine tangled net, tuft or frond of thin vessels lies on the disc or the retinal surface, finer than the arcade it sits on

concepts.question: Is there a dense sheet or pool of blood lying in front of the retina that hides the vessels beneath it, or a diffuse red haze obscuring part of the fundus?

absent.text: the retinal vessels can be followed across the whole frame; nothing dense lies in front of them

present.text: a dense blood sheet, often with a flat upper level, hides the vessels under it, or a red haze veils part of the view

concepts.question: Is there white or grey fibrous, sheet-like or membranous tissue lying on the retinal surface, often over the disc or along the vascular arcades?

absent.text: the retinal surface shows only vessels and orange background, with no opaque sheet lying over it

present.text: an opaque white or grey membranous sheet lies on the retinal surface, often bridging the disc and the arcades
